items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Returns November 24 With Stunning New Release
items.summary: A brand-new Clair Obscur art book is perfect for fans of the series.
items.content:
Image via Sandfall Interactive By Emma Singer Published Oct 4, 2026, 10:57 PM EDT Emma Singer is an Anime & Gaming Editor from New York with over three years of experience writing about media for CBR. Outside of writing, Emma enjoys doing yoga and playing tennis. Sign in to your CBR account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was the best game of 2025, and one of the greatest RPGs of the last decade. The French RPG surprised everyone by selling more than 8 million copies and winning Game of the Year, even with stiff competition. Now, the series is returning with a new artbook that's set to expand the game's world.

The upcoming art book, titled "The Art of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33," is 352 pages and includes both stunning artwork and behind-the-scenes insight into how the extraordinary game was made. It's a truly gorgeous book that's perfect for collectors, and it even comes with lithographs that are perfect for display.

Image via Simon & Schuster On November 24, 2026, Sandfall Interactive's Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 will follow in the footsteps of many other popular video game franchises by receiving its very own art book. Written by Marina Macq, published by UDON Entertainment, and distributed by Simon & Schuster, "The Art of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33" is a new hardcover release, which will be available for $59.99 USD, plus tax and/or shipping.

"Dive into the fascinating video game world of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and discover the secrets behind its remarkable creation in this official artbook," the official description begins . "An unprecedented critical and commercial success, the video game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 captivated more than 3 million players just weeks after its release."

"Created to offer fans and newcomers an engaging look into the creative process behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , this exclusive large-format volume gathers, across more than 350 pages, hundreds of previously unseen documents and illustrations used in the creation of one of the most fascinating games of recent years, including environments, characters, concept art, objects, and more."

"Author Marine Macq, immersed within Sandfall Studio during development, provides a captivating and intimate account of the choices and inspirations that shaped this enchanting universe, from the first sketches to the final renders," the description continues. "To better understand what goes on behind the scenes—and the extraordinary human adventure represented by such an ambitious project—the development team candidly shares the secrets of their experience through a series of fascinating interviews"

Marine Macq is an author and editorial assistant at Pix'n Love and, in 2017, she founded GAMMA, a video game art gallery in France. Pix'n Love has directly collaborated with UDON Entertainment on "The Art of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33", which will include 352 pages of new content.

"The Art of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33" will be available for purchase from Amazon, Barnes & Noble, Bam! Books-A-Million, Bookshop, Hudson Booksellers, Target, and Walmart.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is available to play on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC.

items.title: 2025's Game Of The Year Is Leaving Xbox Game Pass
items.summary: Only a short time remains to finish these nine Xbox Game Pass titles before they're removed.
items.content:
By Nazmul Roosevelt Published Oct 3, 2026, 2:58 PM EDT Nazmul Roosevelt is a journalist who has spent years covering the video games industry with a focus on clarity, accessibility, and genuine curiosity. He works to help players understand the people, craft, and decisions behind the entertainment they love. From game developers, to the technical artists, and communities shaping modern gaming; if you have a story worth sharing, he’s always open to hearing it... And if you happen to know anything about that secret Twin Peaks game in development, he’d especially like to talk. Sign in to your TheGamer account Add Us Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 1 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Nine games are leaving Xbox Game Pass on October 15, 2026. The lineup includes several notable titles across multiple genres and release periods, making this a pretty substantial group of removals. The high‑profile departure to reschedule your time around is unarguably Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . The beloved turn‑based RPG, which has been on Xbox Game Pass since it launched, won Game Of The Year at the 2025 TGAs. Sadly, it will exit the service after nearly eighteen months, marking one of the more significant removals this month.

Another major departure is A Plague Tale: Requiem . This sequel arrived as a day‑one Game Pass release on October 18, 2022. After several years of availability, it will soon leave the subscription catalog, leaving Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy as the only available entry of the series on the service.

The full list of games leaving Xbox Game Pass on October 15 includes:

Donut County, the 2018 Annapurna puzzle classic, rejoined Game Pass in October 2024 and will now jump out of the service a second time. Nova Roma, released on March 26, 2026, is one of the most recent titles leaving the service, having been a part of Game Pass via the Xbox preview program. Superball was a free-to-play game that also had Game Pass benefits added on October 16, 2025.

At the BAFTAs, Charlie Cox and Tracy Wiles were eager to shine a light on their mocap counterparts: Maxence Cazorla and Estelle Darnault.

There's still a lot to flesh out your Halloween for the beginning of October. Crime Scene Cleaner joined on October 1, 2025, following its earlier PC release in August 2024. Pacific Drive was added on October 23, 2025, while The Casting of Frank Stone arrived on October 14, 2025. Evil West entered the service on October 21, 2025, after originally launching in November 2022.

The mix of titles leaving this month is unusually broad. The Casting of Frank Stone, from the creators of Until Dawn , is one of the more underrated horror releases on the service. Pacific Drive offers a survival‑driving experience that built a dedicated audience during its time on Game Pass. Donut County remains a recognizable indie favorite, blending Katamari‑style physics with existential humor. Each of these have shorter playtimes, so the likelihood of you making it to the credits are higher than just now starting Expedition 33.

We speak with one of the 34 Rockstar workers who lost their job last year, in the midst of a high-profile employment tribunal.

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Xbox Game Pass is Losing One of the Best Games Ever This Month
items.summary: Like clockwork, Xbox Game Pass is getting ready to lose another handful of games, and this time the batch includes one of the best games of all time.
items.content:
Xbox Game Pass is Losing One of the Best Games Ever This Month From GameRant (Written by Cameron Swan) on October 3, 2026 | OpenCritic

Xbox Game Pass is losing another collection of games this month, including one of the best titles in recent memory. On October 15, Xbox Game Pass is set to lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the award-winning turn-based RPG from Sandfall Interactive.

In the nine years since Xbox Game Pass' debut, it's become common knowledge that each time the subscription service opens a door to let in a new batch of games, a window opens elsewhere and a handful of games fall out. At the best of times, the games leaving Xbox Game Pass are overshadowed by the ones joining the service that month, but some subscribers might think the losses outweigh the new additions this October. While Xbox Game Pass is getting highly-anticipated titles like Gears of War: E-Day and Valor Mortis this month, it's also losing one of the most acclaimed games of all time.

October's Game Pass lineup is now rolling out, led by an acclaimed title that doubles as an awkward reminder of how much Xbox has changed in 2026.

Rapper T-Pain may just have that affliction, having recently started Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on his Nappy Boy Gaming YouTube channel and noped out after its notoriously sad opening sequence.

*Spoilers for Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 below. Turn back if you haven't played through the prologue yet.*

In the video just below, you can see T-Pain playing about 15 minutes of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 from the very start, which of course means he witnesses the awfully tragic death of Sophie in the prologue, leaving him speechless for a few seconds as he resumes control of Gustave. T-Pain eventually makes an exacerbated "shewwww" sound and exits to desktop. "Is it a sad story?" an offscreen person says, clearly noticing T-Pain's emotional exhaustion. "Yeah."

"Yeah, it was too sad," T-Pain responds, laughing. Just before ending the video, the rapper appears to read a comment on his stream warning him that, "it gets worse" – and anyone who's played through the game knows it absolutely does get worse, and soon – and T-Pain decides then and there, "Absolutely not."

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs were told that "no one" would like one of the RPG's best systems I never want to play the best-written Blood of Dawnwalker mission ever again The AA games industry needs "a few more Expedition 33s," says Valor Mortis director This Game Broke T-Pain - YouTube Watch On I totally get his reluctance to continue here. Sometimes I just want to play a game, or watch a movie, or read a book, and not feel like I need to text my therapist. Unfortunately, in my view, if a story's writing and performances are effective enough to evoke such powerful emotion, it's probably worth seeing through, even if it never provides the sort of emotional upswing you want.

The Last of Us is one of my all-time favorite stories across all mediums precisely because it offers such an uncompromising, realistic account of two normal people trying to navigate a zombie apocalypse. Bad things are going to happen to good people, and there won't always be a picture-perfect redemption for anyone. Casting aside the conventional trajectories of heroes and villains makes for a much more believable, and thus absorbing story. You might not be moving your body like a cyclone afterwards, but you can always get low with something a little lighter to balance things out.

items.title: Clair Obscur Expedition 33 Director Comments on Sandfall's Next Game
items.summary: Sandfall Interactive doesn't seem too worried about living up to GOTY expectations
items.content:
By Polygon Staff & Willa Rowe Published Sep 14, 2026, 1:06 AM EDT FYI Sandfall Interactive doesn't seem too worried about living up to GOTY expectations

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , the debut game from developer Sandfall Interactive, was a smash hit in 2025 and earned numerous game of the year awards . The studio's next project, whatever it may be, might not be as popular. Director Guillaume Broche knows Clair Obscur is a tough act to follow, and he's OK if no one likes what the studio does next.

In a lengthy episode of Video Game Club on the Konbini YouTube channel in July, Broche discusses Sandfall's next game and says, "Maybe people won't like it. That's life." It is a surprisingly laid-back attitude toward following up one of the most beloved games in recent memory. For Broche, it isn't any different from the ethos he and the rest of the team at Sandall Interactive had while making Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . "We didn't make the first game to please anyone," he confesses, "and I think that's why it worked." Rather than pleasing an imaginary audience, Broche reveals that development on Clair Obscur was focused on satisfying the developers. They made a game that excited them. It was just an added bonus that plenty of players enjoyed the game as well.

The process obviously worked, and Broche sees no reason to mess with it, despite mounting expectations brought on by the success of Clair Obscur . He admits that there is definitely pressure to make things bigger or to expand the studio because of the attention Sandfall Interactive now has for its next project. Ultimately, Broche says that this would only result in the studio making games that he doesn't actually want to play.

As for Sandfall's next project, Broche declined to share details but did reveal the team will make some drastic decisions. A big question is whether the studio's next game will be a sequel to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 . In the interview, Broche reiterates the idea he's shared before that "Clair Obscur" is the name of the franchise and Expedition 33 is just one story the team wanted to tell. This could mean Sandfall will take an anthology approach like in Final Fantasy , with each entry introducing a new world and cast of characters. Returning to the world of Expedition 33 in a true sequel would also require Sandfall to choose a canon ending for the game, something the studio has deliberately avoided. In any case, whatever follows Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 will be worth watching.

items.title: Shuhei Yoshida told Expedition 33 studio to avoid terms like 'turn-based RPG' because it may cause people to "overlook" the game
items.summary: The perceived negative stigma around the term 'turn-based RPG' has led Shuhei Yoshida to advise Expedition 33 developers to avoid using it.
items.content:
Image credit: Sandfall / Eurogamer News by Sherif Saed Senior Contributor Published on Aug. 18, 2026, 8:29 a.m. 37 comments Follow Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Prioritise us on Google One of the reasons Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 stood out so much in early footage was how action-packed its combat looked, despite being a turn-based RPG. But while developer Sandfall Interactive has described the game as a turn-based RPG - and reinvigorated the genre, to some degree - not everyone was happy with that approach.

Veteran PlayStation executive Shuhei Yoshida revealed at the Busan Indie Connect Festival 2026 over the weekend that he warned Expedition 33 developers not to give the game that label (via Automaton ).

Yoshida was impressed by the game's combat, likening it to The Legend of Dragoon's, a game he was the producer of. However, his advice was for the team to pick a different term to describe the game, since he believed 'turn-based RPG' is an outdated term to some players, who could end up dismissing the game as a result.

"It's incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG. That alone might cause players to overlook it," Yoshida said, as reported by 4Gamer .

Yoshida, who worked as an advisor to publishers and developers around the time of his departure from PlayStation in 2025 , revealed the anecdote in a panel aimed at helping indie developers pick the right publisher for their games and making a convincing pitch. As part of his consulting work, he worked with Expedition 33 publisher Kepler Interactive, where he got to play a demo of the game two years before its launch.

According to the report, Kepler and Sandfall took his advice, using the more modern 'reactive turn-based battles' term to describe the game's combat instead. As anyone who played the game will attest, Expedition 33's brand of turn-based combat, which melds real-time mechanics like parrying and dodging with traditional turn orders, became one of the strongest and most-lauded aspects of the game .

Regardless of how much you think Yoshida's advice helped, the success of the game is hard to deny. Expedition 33 initially managed to sell a fitting 3.3 million copies in its first month , before bumping that to 5.5 million copies by October 2025.

It's also been one of the highest-rated games of 2025, winning multiple honours at The Game Awards that year, and ending up at number two on Eurogamer's list of the 50 best games of 2025 .

(Image credit: Sandfall Interactive / Kepler Interactive) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 14 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter According to former PlayStation boss Shuhei Yoshida, turn-based RPGs, particularly JRPGs, were so unpopular several years ago that he would tell indie developers to avoid using the term altogether in their marketing—even for a game like Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.

Yoshida recalled giving the Clair Obscur developers this advice during a lecture at the Busan Indie Connect Festival 2026 (via Automaton ). He was impressed by a demo he played a couple of years before the game was out, particularly its similarities to The Legend of Dragoon, a game he produced, but recommended the developers at Sandfall Interactive find alternative ways to describe its combat.

"It's incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG," he said. "That alone might cause players to overlook it."

Sandfall listened and started describing Clair Obscur's combat as "reactive turn-based battles" in its marketing. It's hard to tell if that actually had an impact on the breakout success of the game, but it probably didn't hurt.

Even if you set aside the supposed genre stigma, I think calling Clair Obscur a turn-based RPG does undercut how active the combat actually feels. It isn't the kind of game where you can get up and grab a snack in between turns. You're encouraged to study how enemies move so you can time all your dodges and parries, as if you're playing a soulslike.

Even though turn-based and real time RPGs 'have their loud, vocal advocates,' Fallout developer Tim Cain thinks they both have a place in the genre 'Open world fatigue' is one reason indie RPG Entropy is borrowing from the classics: 'PS1, PS2, GameCube games really never outstayed their welcome' Kingdom Come: Deliverance studio co-founder says a lot of RPGs are 'still games for teenagers,' and that he's 'tired of all the RPGs where you are this chosen one' Did adding a single word before "turn-based" change everything? I'm not convinced it was the sole reason the game caught people's attention when it already looked fast-paced in trailers. But it does speak to the tendency for many games in the genre to only appeal to people who grew up with them, and the number of people who fall asleep when threatened with having to take turns during the action.

Thankfully, Clair Obscur has helped make turn-based games cool again. It sold 3.3 million copies in the first month and has since surpassed eight million copies as of April. Yoshida believes Clair Obscur is a great example of why chasing industry trends isn't always the right move. He also said that publishers have started to see a slew of turn-based games pitched to them in the wake of Clair Obscur's explosive success.

items.title: 'It's Incredibly Well-Made, But…' — Former PlayStation Boss Warned Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Devs It Would Be 'Overlooked' if They Called It a Turn-Based RPG
items.summary: Former PlayStation lead Shuhei Yoshida warned the developers behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 about calling it a "turn-based RPG" because "that alone might cause players to overlook it.
items.content:
Former PlayStation lead Shuhei Yoshida warned the developers behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 about calling it a "turn-based RPG" because "that alone might cause players to overlook it."

Yoshida, who served as PlayStation's head of indies and president of Sony Interactive Entertainment Worldwide Studios before stepping down in 2024, spoke about some key advice he gave the award-winning team during a recent lecture for indie game developers. Portions of that lecture were then reported by 4Gamer and subsequently translated by Automaton , including one piece of advice he gave to publisher Kepler Interactive while advising the team ahead of its April 2025 launch.

"It’s incredibly well-made, but it would be better not to call it a turn-based RPG," Yoshida warned the Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 devs. "That alone might cause players to overlook it."

But why? Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 went on to receive praise from fans and critics (including a 9/10 review from IGN), while ending its already explosive year with big wins across The Game Awards , BAFTA , DICE , and IGN award shows. Its positive reception was so intense that even the developers at Sandfall Interactive weren't prepared for its towering Metacritic score .

Yoshida acknowledged Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 as a quality release long before it reached the hands of the public. He was impressed early on, calling attention to its "combination of turn-based JRPG mechanics and real-time action inputs reminiscent of The Legend of Dragoon." The problem, however, was that, at the time, he was concerned its success could be affected by what he observed to be a tendency for turn-based JRPGs to be seen as outdated.

Game-award-winning formula or not, Yoshida feared Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would be ignored by some gamers if they saw that "turn-based" label. As a result, Kepler got creative and instead started selling Sandfall's first game as an experience with "reactive turn-based battles" instead, and the rest is history.

The game, of course, went on to become a massive sales success despite its proximity to the launch of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion . Yoshida said he's since noticed an uptick in reports from publishers receiving pitches for new turn-based RPGs.

While we wait to see what's next from Yoshida and Sandfall, you can see why the developers behind Final Fantasy Resonance think turn-based RPGs are making a huge comeback . You can also read the devs' conversation about canon endings and the writer who got their start at Sandfall .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

Game Development , Interviews 2026-07-29 00:00 Genki 3 Epic Games Japan and Sandfall Interactive recently hosted a Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 postmortem event in Yokohama, Japan, offering a behind-the-scenes look at the development of 2025’s Game of the Year. After the presentation, AUTOMATON sat down with the developers to discuss their Japanese influences, their views on JRPGs, why Unreal Engine was the right choice for their small team, and why the studio has no intention of significantly increasing its headcount.

Participants are as follows: Guillaume Broche – Sandfall Interactive CEO and Creative Director Tom Guillermin – Sandfall Interactive Co-founder and CTO Alan Reynaud – Lead Character and Concept Artist Alexandre Breton – Technical Artist

For more about Sandfall Interactive’s views on physical disc production ending , check out part two of this interview.

—Could you tell me about the influence Japanese games and anime have had on your approach to game design? What were some of the biggest Japanese influences on Expedition 33?

Guillaume Broche: Growing up, I’d say 95% of the games I was playing were Japanese games, so I’ve always been super influenced by them. My first real video game memory was Final Fantasy VIII on PS1. Before that, I’d also played some games on the Mega Drive, but they were smaller titles and I don’t remember them very well because I was too young. But to this day, JRPGs in particular continue to be one of my favorite genres.

And of course, one of the main influences in my life is the Final Fantasy series and the work of Hironobu Sakaguchi, including titles like Lost Odyssey and Blue Dragon. Other JRPGs that have influenced me include the Shin Megami Tensei and Persona series, the Atelier series, and Tales of Vesperia. I’ve said it a million times by now, but I pretty much play almost all JRPGs available at the time. Not every single one, but really a lot.

Obviously, Expedition 33’s gameplay is very much inspired by the older Final Fantasy games. It’s turn-based, and you have three characters facing three monsters, so they were definitely a massive inspiration.

Also, as I grew up, I think I’d been missing that kind of game ever since Lost Odyssey. Lost Odyssey was, for me, the last big realistic turn-based game. You still have titles like Yakuza and Persona coming out now, but they’re more stylized. On the other hand, I felt like the grand, epic, realistic kind of turn-based games like Final Fantasy X and Last Odyssey didn’t exist anymore. Since that’s my favorite type of game personally, I just wanted to make it.

—How about anime? I believe you’ve mentioned being a big Ghibli fan, but have you drawn influence from any specific titles?

Guillaume Broche: Yes, I know that for a lot of people in the West, Disney is a big part of their childhood memories, but for me, it’s Ghibli. Especially Spirited Away. I think I’ve seen that movie 50 times, no joke. It’s a masterpiece from A to Z, and I also love other films by the studio.

Also, I think one of the anime that inspired me for Expedition 33’s story was Attack on Titan. I really like the idea of a group of heroes fighting together, and I especially love the uniform. When you see any character from Attack on Titan, you instantly know they’re an Attack on Titan character because of the uniform. That’s something I really wanted to bring over into Expedition 33, making the game recognizable just from its uniforms.

In fact, I’m rewatching Attack on Titan right now because I haven’t watched it for at least six years. I’m on season four now, almost at the end, and really, it’s an absolute masterpiece for me.

Alan Reynaud: For the characters, there were a lot of anime that had a big influence on us. One of them is Bleach. I have to mention Bleach because the character designs in the series are spectacular. One of the things we took from it was designs that are super simple yet incredibly memorable. We wanted to have something like that, with a “rule of cool” approach. I’d say that was a big inspiration for the character creation.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
